I fetched nutrition.source_url (weightworld.uk, HTTP 200, real product page, not a search/category page) and parsed the raw HTML rather than trusting a summarizer. All four rows match exactly, each with an empty %NRV cell: Fish Oil 2000 mg; Omega-3 1100 mg; Eicosapentaenoic Acid (EPA) 660 mg; Docosahexaenoic Acid 440 mg. Also confirmed verbatim: "Serving Size: 2 Softgels", "Servings per Container: 120", the footnote "Nutrients Reference Value ... *NRV not established" (so percent_basis "eu" with all percent_dv null, not zero, is right), and "Other Ingredients: Vitamin E (Tocopherol), Gelatin, Glycerol, Purified Water". Zero rows disagree. Independently re-confirmed on weightworld.ie raw HTML: same four rows, same numbers. NOTE - my first pass used WebFetch, whose summarizer HALLUCINATED the .ie DHA row as "Docosahexaenoic Acid (DHA)". The raw HTML shows .ie prints "Docosahexaenoic Acid" with NO abbreviation, same as .uk. So the research's label-asymmetry note is CORRECT and must be honoured: do not "fix" the DHA row by adding (DHA). I nearly filed this as a discrepancy and was wrong to; checking raw HTML is what saved it. 2. PACK SIZE - MATCHES. This was the highest-risk failure mode and it is clean. protein.tn 403s the standard fetcher (Cloudflare), so I re-fetched with a browser UA (HTTP 200, 216KB). h1 and title: "Omega 3 fish oil 240 softgel - weightworld". Its own comparison table row marked "(cette page)" reads brand "weightworld", size "240 capsules molles". Manufacturer variant is 240 softgels ("240 softgels. 4-month supply"). Open Food Facts for GTIN 5056128124017 returns product_name "Omega-3 Fish oil 240 Softgel", brand "WeightWorld", serving "2 softgels". Panel arithmetic corroborates: 120 servings x 2 softgels = 240. Four independent sources converge on 240. No same-brand-different-size substitution. The only other capsule count on our page ("120 capsules") belongs to an unrelated comparison row, TO BOOSTER 120 CAPS. 3. IDENTIFIERS - both verified with my own eyes, contrary to my first grep. The variant JSON on weightworld.uk ties them together in one object: "sku":"CC0350" ... "name":"Omega 3 Fish Oil 2000mg Softgels" ... "barcode":"5056128124017". It is the only barcode on the page. OFF confirms the same GTIN maps to the 240-softgel WeightWorld product. 4. FAQ - ALL SIX SURVIVE. Every answer traces to a fact I confirmed. FAQ 3's "Gluten- and lactose-free formula, suitable for a wide range of dietary and lifestyle needs" is verbatim on the page (I checked because the summarizer omitted it); OFF confirms allergens en:fish and the ingredients text (research wrote "alpha-Tocopheryl", OFF prints the glyph, same substance). FAQ 2's refusal to confirm halal is correct and important: "halal" appears 0 times on the manufacturer page and the gelatin origin is never stated - the FAQ says exactly that instead of guessing. FAQ 4's Advice/Storage text is verbatim on both domains. No FAQ contains a posology: none tells the reader to take anything. FAQ 0 transcribes "Serving Size: 2 softgels" as a label fact, which is the denominator the whole panel depends on, not an instruction; FAQ 4's "ne pas depasser la dose journaliere recommandee" is the standard EU warning and states no number. No FAQ asserts a health claim - the three EFSA benefit statements stay quarantined in claims as attributed quotes with their EFSA footnote, all confirmed on-page. 5. VIDEO - OK. YouTube oEmbed returns author_name "WeightWorld UK" and author_url https://www.youtube.com/@weightworld_uk, with title matching the research character for character. Brand's own channel, not a reviewer upload. 6. DISCARDED CLAIM UPHELD. The research refused to publish the "wild-caught anchovies" sourcing story that search summaries assert. I verified that call: "anchov" and "wild" both appear 0 times on the manufacturer page. Correctly withheld. ONE THING TO REMOVE BEFORE PUBLISH: the claims field asserts, under the header "Manufacturer claims, verbatim", the string "Distilled for pure & contaminant-free omega-3". It is not on the cited source at all, and where it does exist (.ie) it reads "Distilled for contaminant-free omega-3" - "pure &" was added. Strip that one string; the other eight claim strings and all three EFSA benefit statements verified with hit counts on the .uk page.

products.verification:
I tried to break this and could not break the numbers. Every one of the 12 nutrition rows is correct, verified twice against sources I fetched myself.

WHAT I DID. I downloaded the manufacturer's label asset GSW_DRC_5lb_NFP.jpg and read the image directly rather than trusting a text scrape. All 12 rows match to the digit: Calories 120 (no unit on the US panel), Total Fat 1.5g/2%, Sat Fat 1g/5%, Cholesterol 55mg/18%, Sodium 130mg/6%, Total Carb 3g/1%, Dietary Fiber <1g/2%, Total Sugars 1g (no %DV printed), Protein 24g/48%, Calcium 130mg/10%, Iron 0.7mg/4%, Potassium 200mg/4%. Serving 31g (About 1 Scoop), 74 servings/container. Ingredients and «CONTAINS: MILK, SOY.» are verbatim. The three transcription judgment calls are all right: fiber quantity left null instead of rounding <1g up to 1, sugars %DV left null instead of invented, Calories left unitless. Independent cross-check at DPS Nutrition returned an identical row-for-row table.

THE PACK-SIZE TRAP - CLEARED, AND IT WAS A REAL TRAP. The manufacturer hosts separate DRC panels for 2 lb and 5 lb (GSW_DRC_2lb_NFP.jpg and GSW_DRC_5lb_NFP.jpg). I pulled BOTH and compared. They are identical on every per-serving nutrient and differ ONLY in servings per container: 29 vs 74. So the one size-dependent number on the page is 'servings', and the 5 lb panel was correctly used. I then confirmed 74 a third way: protein.tn's own product photo, which I downloaded and read, prints «NET WT 5 LB (2.27 KG)» and «74 SERVINGS». 74 x 31g = 2294g, consistent with 5 lb. No size substitution occurred.

THE US-vs-EU TRAP - ALSO CLEARED. This was the bigger risk, since an EU-market tub carries a per-100g declaration with different figures. The protein.tn photo shows «PROTEIN POWDER DRINK MIX» and the US net-weight format, i.e. the US-labeled tub. Choosing the US Nutrition Facts panel over the EU declaration was the correct call, and the researcher reasoned it out explicitly.

FAQ - ALL SIX SURVIVE. Every factual assertion traces to something I read myself. No entry contains a dosage instruction and no entry contains a health claim. Notably the structure/function claims («to help build and maintain muscle», «5.5g of naturally occurring BCAAs») were kept OUT of the FAQs and confined to the attributed claims field, which is the right separation. FAQ[1] correctly warns the percentages are US Daily Values and not EU reference intakes - that is exactly the kind of thing that misleads a European reader, and it was handled. FAQ[2] survives on its ingredient list but needs one sentence deleted, see dropped[0]. FAQ[4] transparently surfaces the 31g vs 30.4g divergence rather than hiding it; I verified both figures at their respective sources.

VIDEO - CLEAN. YouTube oEmbed returns author_name «Optimum Nutrition», author_url youtube.com/@optimumnutrition. That is the brand's own global channel, not a reviewer. The researcher also correctly rejected an Optimum Nutrition India upload (subsidiary, not the global brand channel) and a third-party creator. official:true stands.

BOTTOM LINE. Publish the nutrition block and all six FAQs after making the five removals in `dropped` and repointing source_url at the label image. The figures a customer would act on - 24g protein, 120 calories, the allergen statement - are solid. My objections are about citation hygiene, one stale-photo contradiction, and an unsubstantiated marketing superlative, not about the numbers.

VERDICT: research CONFIRMED on all four checks. I tried hard to break it and could not. Nothing factual was rejected; my two "dropped" items are compliance strips of accurate content, not error corrections.

1) NUTRITION — VERIFIED. I fetched nutrition.source_url (weightworld.fr) myself: a real product page for this exact item, titled "Glycinate de Magnésium (Bisglycinate) + B6 1422 mg - 180 gélules" — not a search or category page. I checked all three rows, not one, and they match exactly: Magnesium Glycinate 1420 mg (no %), élémentaire 200 mg / 53 %, B6 2 mg / 142 %; Dose journalière 2 gélules; Doses par boîte 90; Autres ingrédients HPMC; no allergen statement. I then cross-checked the UK page independently — it reproduces the panel figure-for-figure in English. I also re-derived the percentages against EU NRVs (375 mg Mg, 1.4 mg B6) and got 53 % and 142 %. No row disagrees.

2) PACK SIZE — VERIFIED, and this was the real risk. protein.tn publishes NO panel and NO format: I confirmed nutrition_values, nutrition_facts, faq, sku, gtin, mpn are all null in the payload, "qte":90 is a stock level (other products on the same page carry qte 17/100/57), and the string "180 gélules" appears NOWHERE in the HTML. So pack size rests entirely on the label image — I downloaded https://admin.protein.tn/storage/produits/oGWKcZXdfbcaJ6SxbL2X9TzwSCqsL2gmBDMFfEYy.webp (the page's own og:image) and read it with my own eyes: "GLYCINATE DE MAGNÉSIUM (BISGLYCINATE) / AVEC VITAMINE B6 / 1422mg PAR PORTION / 180 GÉLULES / 3 MOIS D'APPROVISIONNEMENT / FABRIQUÉ AU ROYAUME-UNI / Sans OGM / Vegan / Sans Stéarate de Magnésium". That matches the FR page's own "180 gélules pour 3 mois d'utilisation" (verified verbatim) and 2x90=180. The same-brand-wrong-size trap was correctly avoided: the US weightworld.com "Magnesium Glycinate 500mg 180 Capsules" also has 180 capsules but a different panel, and it was excluded.

3) FAQ — ALL SIX SURVIVE. Every answer traces to a fact I verified myself. None contains a health claim (the EFSA claims were deliberately kept out and left in nutrition.claims). None issues a dosage instruction: FAQ 0 and 1 mention "2 gélules" only as the nutrition table's reference serving ("la portion de référence", "une dose de 2 gélules apporte"), which is descriptive and unavoidable for reading the panel — neither tells the customer what to take. FAQ 3 is exemplary: it states outright that allergens cannot be confirmed rather than importing third-party "gluten free" text. FAQ 4's two claims are precisely attributed — "FABRIQUÉ AU ROYAUME-UNI" to the label (correct; I verified the manufacturer page does NOT state a country of manufacture) and BPF/HACCP to weightworld.fr, which I confirmed verbatim: "Contrôle qualité : Produit élaboré selon les normes européennes BPF et HACCP pour les compléments alimentaires."

4) VIDEO — OK, brand-owned, proven bidirectionally. ytInitialPlayerResponse gives channelId UCvNzwO2IebamOFBMInBRzmA, ownerChannelName "WeightWorld UK", canonicalBaseUrl /@weightworld_uk; the weightworld.uk homepage links out to youtube.com/@weightworld_uk. Same channel both directions, so not a reviewer upload. Caveat to carry forward: the video is a general brand piece on magnesium glycinate, shows no panel and cites no figures — it sourced zero data, so it is decorative only.

INFRASTRUCTURE WARNING (unrelated to the research, but do not ship without reading): my FIRST curl of the product URL returned HTTP 200 with a COMPLETELY DIFFERENT PRODUCT — "<title>100% WHEY PROTEIN 2.27KG - CHALLENGER NUTRITION</title>", with zero occurrences of "bisglycinate". The immediate retry returned the correct magnesium page. Response headers show cf-cache-status: EXPIRED, x-nextjs-cache: STALE, and Vary: rsc, next-router-state-tree, ... — i.e. Cloudflare is keying/serving cache across a Vary header set it ignores, so this URL can serve another product's page to a real user or crawler. This matches the known cloudflare-vary-is-ignored and build-403 issues. Verification of the product data is unaffected (I confirmed against the manufacturer and the label image), but publishing enriched content onto a URL that intermittently serves someone else's product is worth escalating separately.

VERDICT: the numbers are real, but they are the wrong generation's numbers for this bag. Publish only the hedged subset.

NUTRITION - VERIFIED AS A TRANSCRIPTION (verified_nutrition: true). I fetched the source, found the embedded label JSON, and checked all 34 rows, not a sample. Every one matches byte-for-byte allowing decimal-comma to decimal-point: Energy "5279 kJ/1262 kcal", Fat "7,0 g", saturates "3,9 g", Carbohydrates "248 g", sugars "11 g", Fibre literally "- g" (correctly rendered as undeclared), Protein "50 g", Salt "1,17 g", and all 26 compositionTable rows including Iron "18 mg (127%)*", Copper "1,3 mg (134%)*", Iodine "150 µg (100%)*", Creatine "3,0 g". Column heading "2 scoops (336 g)" confirmed; the untranscribed "100 g" column confirmed to exist. The footnote "* Reference intake of an average adult (8400 kJ / 2000 kcal)" is real (emitted when showReferenceIntake is true, which it is for the compositionTable) - percent_basis "eu" is correct. Ingredients, mayContainAllergens [gluten, egg, nuts, peanuts], allergenContainment SEE_INGREDIENTS, labelWarnings, storageAdvice and legalName all verbatim. Zero fabrication; the researcher's transcription discipline was excellent.

PACK SIZE - MATCHES. Manufacturer has "Serious Mass Weight Gainer Protein Powder - Chocolate / 5.45 kg (16 servings)" and the Chocolate record's variantLabelData carries 1101529 and 1151655, both "5450 grams ℮" / "16 servings". protein.tn's title, canonical and product photo all read 5,45 kg / 12 LB / 16 SERVINGS. No same-brand-wrong-size error here. The consistency check holds too: 16 x 336 g = 5376 g, close to the 5450 g net.

THE ACTUAL DEFECT - FORMULA GENERATION. The panel is ON's 2024 reformulation (the source record is titled "...Chocolate Flavor - Reformulation"). Three independent signals say protein.tn is selling the older bag: its own product image prints 1,250 CALORIES / 252g CARBS; its own French copy sells the product on "caseine", "proteines d'oeuf" and "glutamine", none of which exist in the current formula; and OFF 5060245600453 for this exact 5.45 kg chocolate bag returns 1260 kcal / 252 g carbs with L-Glutamine and Glutamine Peptides. The research flagged this itself and was right to - I am upholding its caveat as a blocker, not a footnote.

FAQ - 3 of 6 SURVIVE: [0, 4, 5]. Kept: 0 (net content / servings - independently corroborated by the physical bag photo, and stable across both generations), 4 (explains the EU reference-intake basis - pure meta, no variant-dependent number), 5 (the flavour/photo mismatch disclaimer - I verified every assertion in it, including that the photo is a Strawberry bag printing 1,250 cal and 252 g carbs). Dropped 1, 2, 3 - see dropped[]. FAQ[2] is the serious one: it downgrades egg from a probable declared ingredient to a "may contain" trace, on a page whose own description says the product contains egg protein. No surviving entry carries a dosage instruction or a health claim; the recommendedUsage sentence ("Add two heapings scoops... 710 ml of water") was correctly excluded throughout.

VIDEO - CORRECTLY OMITTED (video_ok: true). I re-ran oEmbed on all five candidates and every one is a third-party uploader, exactly as reported: monstersupplements, Buyer's Edge, BroScience Bodybuilding, Jonathan Cantley, Weight Gain Network. No ON brand-channel video exists for this product and none is being published, so there is nothing to reject.

SEPARATE ESCALATION: I reproduced the wrong-content-served bug and it is broader than reported - a cache-busted request to this product URL returned the ANABOLIC WHEY 80 2.25kg - ProActive page with that product's title and canonical, a different wrong product than the researcher hit. Six retries were needed to get the right page. Canonicals and Product JSON-LD are being served for the wrong products at real URLs.

RECOMMENDATION: do not publish the nutrition panel as this product's panel until someone photographs a bag from protein.tn's actual stock. If the panel must ship now, ship it attributed and hedged exactly as FAQ[5] does, drop the allergen FAQ entirely, and fix the Strawberry photo on a chocolate listing regardless.
problems: NOT A TRANSCRIPTION ERROR - A PROVENANCE ERROR. All 34 rows are verbatim-correct against the manufacturer source, but the panel describes ON's 2024 reformulation while every signal on protein.tn points at the pre-reformulation bag. Confirmed independently by me: (a) protein.tn's product image (https://admin.protein.tn/storage/produits/February2026/ZM8A9ZkKwfpYgqKRpsO3.webp) is an old-style bag reading 'STRAWBERRY FLAVOR / NET WT 5.45 kg (12 LB) / 16 SERVINGS / 1,250 CALORIES / 50g PROTEIN / 252g CARBS'; (b) protein.tn's own French copy lists 'caseine', 'proteines d'oeuf' and 'glutamine', none of which appear in the current panel; (c) OFF 5060245600453 for the 5.45 kg chocolate bag returns 1260 kcal / 252 g carbs with Choline Bitartrate, L-Glutamine and Glutamine Peptides in the ingredients. The source record is even literally titled 'Optimum Nutrition - Serious Mass - Chocolate Flavor - Reformulation'. Do not publish the panel as this bag's panel without a photo of a physical bag from protein.tn's stock.

ALLERGEN DELTA IS THE REAL HAZARD. The two formula generations differ in allergen class, not just numbers: current = whey protein concentrate only, with egg as 'may contain'. Pre-reformulation = whey + calcium caseinate + EGG ALBUMIN, i.e. egg as a declared ingredient. Publishing the current allergen statement against the old bag understates egg from an ingredient to a trace. This is the single highest-consequence error in the payload.

CITED URL REDIRECTS. nutrition.source_url (https://www.optimumnutrition.com/en-ie/Products/Weight-Gainers/Serious-Mass/p/serious-mass) 301s to https://www.optimumnutrition.com/products/serious-mass-weight-gainer-protein-powder-eu. It resolves 200 and carries the data, but store the resolved URL as the citation so the reference does not rot.

PANEL IS PER-FLAVOUR, NOT PER-PACK. products.verification: Verified independently; the research holds up, with fixes required before publish. NUTRITION (verified true): I fetched the raw HTML of the cited OFF page for barcode 6224009363018 — it is a genuine product page and its 'As sold per serving (34 g) (packaging)' column matches all ten submitted rows verbatim (135 kcal, fat 2 g, sat fat 1 g, cholesterol 0.045 g, carbs 5 g, sugars 1.5 g, fiber 0.5 g, protein 24 g, salt 0.125 g, sodium 0.05 g). Zero rows disagree. The 100 g column is confirmed to be OFF's own recalculation (protein 70.5882352941177 g) and must never ship. PACK SIZE (matches): protein.tn sells title '100% WHEY PROTEIN 2.27KG', body '2,27 kg', aroma Chocolat; the manufacturer's variant JSON gives weight 2268 g with a single Default Title variant under the page title '100% Whey Protein (Egypt Edition)'; Maxmuscle Elite ties barcode [6224009363018] to Weight 2.267KG / 66 servings / Chocolate / Origin Egypt. 2268/34 = 66.7 ≈ 66 servings, internally consistent. I computed the EAN-13 check digit myself (sum 62 → check 8, valid) and confirmed GS1 prefix 622 = Egypt. CORROBORATION: because OFF is crowd-sourced and carries no nutrition label photo, I cross-checked two independent retailers — iFit-eg and MyOras both publish 34 g / 24 g protein / 2 g fat / 5 g carbs / 1.5 g sugars, identical to OFF. The protein figure, the one a customer acts on, is now backed by four independent sources. The remaining five rows rest on OFF alone. VIDEO (rejected): oEmbed returns author_name 'Matt Chambers' at @mattchambers4862 — a reviewer upload, not the brand. Challenger Nutrition has no YouTube channel. FAQ: all six survive. Each is source-backed and I verified the load-bearing quotes against the originals — the Maxmuscle warnings text came back word-for-word identical, the manufacturer's 'whey protein concentrate, and whey protein hydrolysate' and the '(Egypt Edition)' title are verbatim from the page I fetched, and Origin: Egypt / Company: Challenger Nutrition are confirmed. None contains a dosage instruction (notably, Maxmuscle's 'one scoop in 125-200 ml' was correctly left out) and none carries a health claim (the manufacturer's 'for maximum strength and performance' was correctly truncated). MUST FIX BEFORE PUBLISH: (1) the nutrition.claims field carries unauthorized health claims — 'improve cardiovascular and immune functioning', 'Energy Booster', 'stimulates protein synthesis' — and must not render; (2) servings_per_container, net_quantity and warnings are attributed to source_url but are not on that page — re-attribute or drop; (3) add an explicit allergen notice, since no source publishes ingredients and this is a milk-derived product; (4) do not write the third-party GTIN into our schema.org markup, as our own record has gtin:null. This research was unusually disciplined — it discarded the 100 g column, three contradicting retailers, and its own video find, and every one of those calls was correct.
problems: ATTRIBUTION MISMATCH (fix before publish): nutrition.source_url points at Open Food Facts, but servings_per_container ('66'), net_quantity (2.267 kg) and warnings do NOT appear on that page. The OFF entry has an EMPTY quantity field. Those values came from Maxmuscle Elite / Yankeesta. I independently confirmed they are TRUE (Maxmuscle: Weight 2.267KG, Servings 66; manufacturer JSON: weight 2268 g; iFit: 2.267 kg / 66 servings) — so the numbers are right, but the citation is wrong. Re-attribute per-field or drop them from the nutrition object.

PACK-SIZE LINK IS INDIRECT: the cited OFF page shows no net weight and no flavor. Its product name is only 'Whey Protein - Challenger' (brand recorded as 'Challenger', not 'CHALLENGER NUTRITION'). The tie to our 2.27 kg Chocolat tub rests entirely on the barcode appearing on a third-party retailer page. It holds up (barcode check digit valid, GS1 622 = Egypt, manufacturer weight 2268 g, 2268/34 = 66.7 servings), but nothing on the cited page itself states the size. Mitigating factor: per-serving values for a powder do not vary by tub size — iFit publishes the identical panel for both the 1 kg and 2.267 kg packs — so a wrong-size panel is a low-probability failure here.

OFF HAS NO NUTRITION LABEL PHOTO: I checked the raw HTML — zero nutrition images. The panel is crowd-entered text tagged '(packaging)' with no image to audit it against. 5 of 10 rows (serving 34 g, protein 24 g, fat 2 g, carbs 5 g, sugars 1.5 g) are independently corroborated by iFit-eg and MyOras. The other 5 rows — energy 135 kcal, saturated fat 1 g, cholesterol 0.045 g, fiber 0.5 g, salt 0.125 g / sodium 0.05 g — rest on OFF ALONE and are unverifiable. Saturated fat is actively contested (MightyGains says 1.5 g). Consider publishing only the corroborated rows.

ALLERGEN GAP ON A MILK PRODUCT: OFF states 'Ingredients are missing' (confirmed in raw HTML) and the allergens field is empty. No source publishes an ingredient list. Publishing a whey protein page with no allergen statement is the one genuine consumer-safety weakness here. The research was right not to fabricate a declaration, but the page should carry an explicit 'consult the packaging for allergens' notice rather than silence.

GTIN IS NOT OURS: our own product record returns "gtin":null,"sku":null,"nutrition_images":[] (verified in the page's embedded JSON; sku is the internal id 439). The barcode 6224009363018 is sourced only from third parties. Do NOT write it into our schema.org Product markup as our gtin without packaging confirmation — a wrong GTIN in structured data is a Merchant Center problem.
ENERGY ROW: OFF's per-serving cell literally reads '? kcal (135 kcal)' — the kJ value is absent. Publish 135 kcal only; do not derive kJ.
percent_basis is empty — no %DV or NRV on the cited page. Do not let any template infer daily values.
